content: Marrubium vulgare, commonly known as White Horehound or Common Horehound, is a flowering plant that belongs to the family Lamiaceae. It is native to regions of Europe, northern Africa, and Asia. This plant is a greyish-leaved, herbaceous perennial that bears a resemblance to mint in its appearance. It typically grows to a height of 25 to 45 centimeters. The leaves of Marrubium vulgare are between 2 and 5 centimeters in length. They have a densely crinkled surface and are covered with fine, downy hairs. The flowers of this plant are white in color and grow in clusters located on the upper portion of the main stem. Like other plants in the Lamiaceae family, White Horehound has a distinctive square-shaped stem. Historically, White Horehound has been utilized in the production of cough remedies and hard candies. Additionally, Marrubium vulgare has agricultural applications, as it is used as a natural repellent for grasshoppers. The plant is also associated with a specific insect known as the Horehound bug, which commonly feeds on White Horehound.
